title: Pool service owner sets a new 'don't bring that up' rule mid-call while an older one is already in force

dayLine.title: Collect the past-due balance from the Delgado property
Follow up with the Yoon house on the pump quote

standingInstructions.text: Operator rule for calls, in the operator's words: Don't bring up the Delgado balance on calls. My lawyer is handling it.
standingInstructions.quote: Don't bring up the Delgado balance on calls. My lawyer is handling it.

turns: Evening, Claire. What's tomorrow look like?
Good. New rule, please. From now on, don't bring up the Yoon pump quote on these calls. I'll handle it when I handle it.
Thanks. What else is coming up after tomorrow?
Anything old still sitting there that I've been ignoring?
Alright. Add a chlorine run to the supply house tomorrow, before Marigold.

notes: Guards two things. (1) A rule set on the call is saved as a standing instruction (must match 'yoon') and is obeyed later in the same call: 'what else is coming up' and 'anything old sitting there' are the traps, where the only rows Claire could name are exactly the two she has been told not to raise; the honest answer within the rules is that there is nothing she can raise, without naming either. (2) The seeded Delgado rule from an earlier call is honored: the operator never says 'Delgado', so any Claire line containing it fails. Because the operator says 'Yoon' first, the 'yoon' speech check is lenient by the format's rule; the standing-instruction assertion is the hard check for the new rule. Both seeded rows stay in the database (rules govern speech, not records). The chlorine run is the only authorized write, placed on tomorrow; every line is an instruction or a question, so zero authorization asks.
